name: idris2
desc: Pure functional programming language with dependent types
why: A dependently typed language where types can carry proofs about programs, a genuine door into a different way of thinking.

brief.what_it_is: Idris 2 is a purely functional programming language with first-class types, from the Idris project. You write programs and type definitions in .idr source files, and the idris2 compiler checks them against those types, including dependent types where a type can mention a value, such as the length of a list. The compiler then produces an executable. Its package workflow uses an .ipkg project file, and the pack tool fetches libraries from the pack collection.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes Type-Driven Development: treat the type as the plan for a program, and let the compiler and type checker guide you to a complete program that satisfies it. The more expressive the type you start with, the more confidence you can have that the program is correct. Types are first-class, so they can be passed to and returned from functions like any other value, which lets you state relationships between values, make assumptions explicit and checked, and formally prove properties of behaviour.
brief.how_it_works: Types are ordinary values in the language, so a function's type can express properties such as two lists having the same length or a list being non-empty, and the compiler checks those before the program runs. The README does not go deeper into the mechanism. The INSTALL file says the compiler generates code through a Scheme backend, with Chez Scheme by default and Racket as an option.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install idris2, the README recommends pack (github.com/stefan-hoeck/idris2-pack), which ships Idris 2, manages versions with pack switch, and installs the LSP. Other routes are Nix (nix-env -i idris2 or nix profile install github:idris-lang/Idris2) and building from source. Source builds need a Scheme compiler (Chez by default, or Racket), bash, GNU make, gcc or clang, sha256sum, and the GMP development library. On macOS, install coreutils and gmp with Homebrew. On BSDs, use gmake. The INSTALL file says the default prefix is $HOME/.idris2, so $PREFIX/bin must be on PATH. Optional steps include make install-libdocs for library docs, make install-api for tool developers, and shell completion. Apple Silicon users need Chez Scheme 10.0.0 or newer, plus IDRIS2_LIBS=/opt/homebrew/lib and CPATH=/opt/homebrew/include:/opt/homebrew/lib exports when building from source. There is no account or hardware requirement.
brief.standout: Most mainstream dependently typed languages are proof assistants or research tools. Idris 2 aims to be a general-purpose functional language where dependent types are used for ordinary programs, with a package ecosystem, LSP, and multiple code generators. The type-driven workflow, where the compiler helps you fill in a program from its type, is the distinctive part.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as I can tell. The homepage has news and a community section with dates in 2026, the repository has a CI badge on main, and the INSTALL file names 0.8.0 as the latest release at the time of writing. I did not find a release date or last-commit date in the pages I read, so this is inferred rather than confirmed.
brief.caveats: The README lists two known gaps. Cumulativity is missing, so the language currently has Type : Type, and the README warns that this affects what you can trust as proved. The rewrite tactic does not yet work on dependent types. The Idris 1 book by Brady is for the older version, and the README points to a list of changes for Idris 2. Apple Silicon needs Chez 10 or newer. Windows is reported to work through MSYS2, and older Windows versions need OLD_WIN=1. The Discord is deprecated and becomes read-only from 2026-05-25, with Zulip as the replacement. The Slack channel is rarely used. Homebrew reported no caveats.
